skill.name: scanning-tools
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through network discovery, vulnerability assessment, web application scanning, wireless testing, cloud checks, compliance scans, and reporting.
skill.summary: Operational reference for authorized security scanning workflows across networks, web apps, wireless systems, cloud accounts, and compliance checks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms substantial high-risk scanning and exploitation guidance throughout SKILL.md, including Nmap, Masscan, Aircrack-ng, Metasploit, sudo-driven tools, and active web scanners. Several Markdown backtick detections are documentation artifacts, but the skill still instructs users to run intrusive commands and includes critical Internet-scale scanning and exploit validation workflows. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Metasploit launch, module, target, run, and exploit suggestion steps, or replace them with non-exploit validation guidance.
Remove 0.0.0.0/0 Masscan examples and require explicit written scope before any network scanning guidance.
Remove deauthentication, handshake cracking, and WEP cracking commands; keep only passive inventory guidance for authorized labs.
Reduce sudo usage, remove destructive file deletion examples, and document least-privilege execution and safe output locations.

remediation.issue: Active scanner commands without enforceable safety gates
remediation.suggestion: Add mandatory authorization, scope, rate limit, and maintenance-window checks before showing active web or network scan commands.

content.value_statement: Security teams need consistent workflows for scanning authorized systems without missing common checks. This skill organizes tool choices, commands, reporting steps, and validation guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Maps scanning goals to tools such as Nmap, Masscan, Nessus, OpenVAS, ZAP, Nikto, Lynis, and OpenSCAP.
Provides command examples for host discovery, port scanning, service detection, web scanning, wireless testing, and compliance checks.
Outlines a phased methodology from planning and authorization to reporting and remediation guidance.
Summarizes output formats and report generation options for common scanners.
Lists troubleshooting steps for host discovery, scan speed, and web scanner coverage.
limitations: It does not verify that a target is authorized or in scope.
It can produce intrusive scans that may disrupt systems or trigger alerts.
It does not replace manual validation by a qualified security professional.
Tool availability, licensing, and platform support vary by environment.

use_cases.title: Plan Internal Vulnerability Scans
use_cases.description: Create a scoped scan plan that covers discovery, service enumeration, vulnerability checks, and reporting for approved assets.

use_cases.title: Prepare Web Application Testing
use_cases.description: Select web scanning tools, define crawl and active test boundaries, and organize findings for remediation review.

use_cases.title: Collect Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Use compliance scanners and reporting steps to gather evidence for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, or internal control reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Check Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authorized scan scope, time window, and tool list. Identify missing prerequisites and low-impact starting checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Scan Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a practical workflow for known assets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased security scan plan for these approved assets: [asset list]. Include discovery, vulnerability checks, validation, and reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Scanner Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these authorized scanner findings. Group duplicates, flag likely false positives, and prioritize issues by business impact.

prompt_templates.title: Design An Assessment Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a recurring scanning program for my organization. Include scope controls, safe scan windows, evidence handling, reporting, and escalation rules.

output_examples.input: Create a scan plan for an approved internal subnet and a web application.
output_examples.output: A phased plan with authorization checks, host discovery, web crawler boundaries, vulnerability validation, evidence handling, and reporting milestones.
An executive summary with risk themes, affected systems, business impact, remediation owners, and follow-up validation steps.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot a scan that missed expected hosts.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering scope confirmation, firewall behavior, discovery methods, DNS settings, scanner timing, and connectivity verification.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before any scan.
Start with low-impact discovery, then increase intensity only when approved.
Record tool versions, time windows, targets, and evidence for every assessment.
anti_patterns: Scanning public or third-party targets without written permission.
Using high-rate or intrusive scans during business hours without coordination.
Publishing raw scan output that includes secrets, internal addresses, or exploitable details.

faq.question: Does this skill run scans automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow and command guidance that users may apply in their own authorized environment.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for security professionals working within a clearly authorized assessment scope.

faq.question: Can it validate scan results?
faq.answer: It can help organize validation steps, but a qualified reviewer must confirm findings and business impact.

faq.question: Does it include web application scanning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Nikto, crawl planning, active testing, and report generation.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: The guidance includes intrusive scanners, privileged commands, wireless attacks, and exploit validation examples.

faq.question: Can it support compliance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It references tools and workflows for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, Lynis, OpenSCAP, and evidence reporting.
